key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term perovskite photoluminescence degradation from early-time spectra, enabling faster stability assessment of unseen materials.
engineering_relevance: This could substantially shorten accelerated aging campaigns for perovskite solar materials while providing interpretable stability descriptors for materials screening.
method: Collected 86k+ photoluminescence spectra from 167 metal halide perovskites under heat and light stress.
Converted spectra into physics-informed features to capture degradation behavior and improve explainability.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM model to predict future PL intensity for samples not seen during training.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on a diverse dataset spanning different crystallinities and compositions, and it outperformed baseline benchmarks while generalizing across material groups.
watch_item: Forecast quality may depend on how well the training data cover new perovskite chemistries, stress conditions, and measurement protocols.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
